title: Splitting the flock
_map: Splitting the flock (Y1–2). Big idea: number bonds, 10 can be split into two parts in set ways; the pattern; then 20.
_story: Steve built two fields but can't decide how to share 10 sheep. He finds every way, spots the pattern (one up, one down), catches Steve losing a sheep in its sums, then tries 20.
_stepChain: counting → 10 sheep, two fields → split them any way → every split still makes 10 → named number bonds → the pattern → Steve's mistake (6 and 3) → 20 sheep

talk.ask: How many ways can 10 sheep go into two fields?
talk.goodAnswer: 11 ways, from 0 and 10 up to 10 and 0. Every way still makes 10.

talk.ask: When one field gets one more sheep, what happens to the other one?
talk.goodAnswer: it gets one fewer, so the total stays 10.

handsOn: Take 10 Lego bricks and two bowls. Find every way to share them, and line the ways up in order: 0 and 10, 1 and 9 … What pattern do you see?

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I built two fields with fresh grass! I've got 10 sheep. But I can't decide how many should go in each field. Will you help me try different ways?
Choose how many sheep go into the first field, then tap the hammer. The rest go into the other field. How many different ways can you find?
Every single way still makes 10 sheep. 4 and 6. 7 and 3. Even 0 and 10. Pairs of numbers that make 10 like this are called number bonds.
Here's a pattern. Move one sheep from this field to that one. One field goes up by one, and the other goes down by one. So the total never changes.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: I've got it! I put 6 sheep in the first field and 3 sheep in the other field. That's all 10 sheep!

question.onRight: Yes, you caught it. 6 and 3 make only 9, so one sheep is missing.

0.mistake: didn't check that the two parts add back up to 10
0.hint: Count them up: 6, then 3 more. Do you get to 10?
0.say: Count on from 6: 7, 8, 9. That's only 9 sheep. One sheep is still wandering about! With 6 in the first field, the other field needs 4.

question.reveal: 6 and 4 make 10. Steve forgot one sheep!

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Oops, thank you! Now, I'm getting more sheep. 20 of them!

question.prompt: How many ways can 20 sheep go into two fields? Make a guess.
question.reveal: 21 ways, from 0 and 20 all the way to 20 and 0. With 10 sheep there were 11 ways. With 20 sheep there are 21. Always one more than the number of sheep.

rule.text: Split 10 any way: the parts still make 10.
rule.ask: Can you say what stays the same, however you split the sheep? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: However you split 10, the two parts still make 10. Those pairs are called number bonds.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: what if there were three fields? Guess how many ways 10 sheep could go into three fields.
bonus.reveal: 66 ways! One more field makes lots more ways. That's a puzzle mathematicians love.
